newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher, helped by GCA stock data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher, helped by GCA stock data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday, as the market rebounded from recent sharp losses after the release of supportive monthly stock figures, traders said.
Benchmark September arabicas closed 9.10 cents per lb higher, at 190.70, after ranging from 194.00 to 181.60. Spot July jumped 12.20 cents, to 208.70, while the back months rose 6.20 to 8.50.
The July/September switch widened to 18.00 cents at the close, from 14.90 cents on Monday.
Arabica prices rose at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, after a smaller-than-expected increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks in May prompted commission house buying, traders said.

The Green Coffee Association of New York reported after the close on Monday stocks of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouse increased in May by 122,000 60-kg bags, to 1,977,000 bags. Most industry participants had expected a build of some 200,000 bags.

"(GCA) rise was very modest," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "So, we are still looking at limited stocks. We had seen the market come off more than $1 and this stopped the deterioration and reminded everyone that, fundmentally, supplies are tight."
Technically, traders said the market had been due for a bounce after falling about 14 percent last week in anticipation of a U.S. stock build up and a bearish USDA world coffee production report.
"The market came down hard enough," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "I think it over-reacted to the USDA figures."

The USDA data, released late Friday, put Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop at 28 million 60-kg bags, up from a revised 27.5 million in 1996/97. USDA pegged world 1997/98 production at 103.7 million versus 100.7 million in 1996/97.
On Tuesday, the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said it would welcome clarification from the USDA over methodology of its latest coffee supply estimates.
The ACPC said its members were concerned over the USDA forecast which it said differed vastly from the recent production number released by some governments.
On the charts, traders said the 200.00-cent level would present a major test of resistance for the September contract. Support was seen at 185.00 cents.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 500 bags as of June 16, to 47,550 bags. There were 1,539 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
